speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your condition, could you please describe when the blisters and ulcers first appeared and if you have experienced any fever, fatigue, or joint pain recently? Also, have you started any new medications or had any recent sun exposure?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. I need to clarify the nature of the mucosal ulcers: have you noticed any sores specifically inside your mouth, such as on the gums or roof of the mouth, or are the symptoms limited to the areas you mentioned? Also, do the blisters on your forearm appear only in areas exposed to sunlight?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of painful oral and genital ulcers alongside skin blisters raises concern for autoimmune blistering diseases like pemphigus vulgaris or mucous membrane pemphigoid. I need to check for specific oral signs and request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis.
